open_threads: MY READ, NOT RATIFIED, on each of these. (1) THE BET THIS TICKET DID NOT PROVE: naming the denied capability is supposed to invert the maintenance — the closure grows freely while the denied set sits still. That needs corpus time, so it left as the WATCHME rather than a criterion, with a baseline written down as provenance (closure 17 modules, denied 13, both measured 2026-08-12 by the same walk the probe runs). The probe fires on the FIRST gain and clears only when the set is unchanged AND ten distinct modules have entered the closure — the denominator exists because zero growth against zero closure movement is the misaimed census the librarian already taught us. (2) TWO PREDICTIONS THIS VOYAGE KILLED with measurements rather than arguments, both worth carrying: _SOLE_PATH does NOT cover the inference host for this purpose (planting `import cairn.devices.inference_domain.route` leaves it GREEN — inference_domain is precisely the component permitted to dial — while the verdict path gains the ability to ask an LLM; WHO MAY DIAL and WHAT A VERDICT MAY REACH are different questions); and the new sieve does NOT mirror sole_path_holds' per-row attribution — doing so rebuilt a 243-file graph 24 times, added 22s per inspection and timed out this component's own proof, and re-read afterwards the analogy was wrong on the merits too, since sole_path binds every component while this binds one path. (3) STILL OPEN AND NAMED RATHER THAN FIXED: the dynamic-import check in test_inspector_nexus.py names 5 modules by hand while the closure holds 17 (recorded in the proof as a residue, not widened — out of this ticket's bounds); a subprocess dials and imports nothing, and a dynamic import is invisible to the walk (filed edge (b) on the ticket, unchanged); a dotted name resolving to no file is a dead end of the walk, safe only while every denied capability is an in-tree module (filed edge (a)).
